properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Dona Ana County in south central New Mexico...

* Until 1145 PM MDT.

* At 833 PM MDT, Thunderstorms with very heavy rainfall have
affected a broad swath of rural southwestern Dona Ana County.

flooding is likely to occur on back roads north and south of
Interstate 10, west of the Border Patrol Checkpoint, and east of
the Luna County line. This includes County Highway C-001, and
possibly the I-10 frontage roads in the vicinity of Exit 116.

producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
mainly rural areas of West Central Dona Ana County.

The Mason Draw drainage area has been particularly hard hit.

properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 1 at 8:22PM MDT until August 1 at 10:30PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
At 822 PM MDT, Light to moderate rain is moving back over the
Tularosa Creek basin, but is not expected to exacerbate flooding.
However, flooding has occurred on the creek. The peak flow reached
the river gauge at Gato Mountain Road around 5:45 PM, and reached
Tularosa Falls around 7 PM. High flows will work their way
downstream towards low water crossings around Tularosa in the next
few hours.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, low water
crossings, and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Tularosa.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
